column1: #   ok:any:MINCHARS        extraction must succeed with >= MINCHARS chars, any method
#   ok:METHOD:MINCHARS     extraction must succeed via METHOD (trafilatura|json-ld|regex|pdftotext) with >= MINCHARS
#   fail                   must fail gracefully (non-zero exit / error result, no garbage content)
# Lines starting with # are rationale, not tests. Thresholds are set at
# roughly 40-50% of the measured baseline so page edits don't false-alarm;
# a drop below them means real content loss. Run with: webx --selftest
# Baseline: 2026-08-02 gauntlet run (20 URLs, 17 extracted, 3 graceful fails).
# --- trafilatura path: standard articles, blogs, news ---
# Wikipedia (special case: plain HTML pipeline; JSON API alternative documented in skill)
# Wikipedia large page: stresses 2MB+ download and very long extraction
# NVIDIA corporate blog (was a trafilatura 0-byte case on this box)
# Custom static site (primeradiant; trafilatura 0-byte case elsewhere)
# Short link-blog post (2.8K is the FULL post, not truncation)
# Landing page (intentionally thin — intro + feature list)
# --- json-ld path: paywalled article with publisher-declared articleBody ---
# HBR paywall: trafilatura only sees the summary (423 chars); json-ld has the full body
# --- regex path: paywall / wrong-content WordPress / huge papers ---
# WordPress where trafilatura grabs wrong content; regex must win
# X/Twitter post (fragile — X changes often; low threshold)
# Anthropic research page (plain curl blocked; curl-cffi rescue or direct 200)
# --- graceful failures (must exit non-zero with a clear reason, never garbage) ---
# PubMed is a FLAKY reCAPTCHA wall: sometimes the curl-cffi rescue slips
# through (real abstract extracted), sometimes the wall holds (graceful fail
# with a captcha hint). Both outcomes are correct behavior for webx, so this
# case is excluded from the strict suite to keep it deterministic. Re-enable
# manually if you want to probe it: expect fail is the conservative baseline.
# kyutai blog is a Next.js CSR shell — content absent from static HTML
# YouTube is a video, not an article (use youtube-content skill / fetch_transcript.py)
# Styled 404 (HBR returns 200-status page with "Sign In / Go back")
